Managing Employee Records Using Structures

Problem Statement:
You are tasked with developing a simple employee management system for a small company. Each employee has the following information:

Name (a string)
Age (an integer)
Salary (a floating-point number)
You need to define a structure called Employee that contains these three members. Your task is to read and store information for n employees, then print the employee details in a formatted way. You will also be required to find and display the details of the employee with the highest salary.

Input:
The first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100), representing the number of employees.
The next n lines each contain the employee details: a string name, an integer age, and a floating-point salary.

Output:
Print the details of all employees in the format: Name: , Age: , Salary: .
Print the details of the employee with the highest salary in the format: Highest Salary -> Name: , Age: , Salary: .

constraints:
The employee name will not exceed 100 characters.
The age of an employee will be between 18 and 65.
The salary will be a floating-point number in the range of 3000.0 to 100000.0.
You must use structures to define and store employee information.
Dynamically allocate memory to store the employee records.
